title: Parser ignores the importer's number format
presentedFailure: NumberFormatException 'Character , is neither a decimal digit number, decimal point, nor "e" notation exponential mark.' from BigDecimal, called by AmountParser.parse (line 9) with the text "1.234,50".
knownRootCause: AmountParser.parse passes the raw text to new BigDecimal(...), which only understands a dot decimal and no thousands separator. The spec requires accepting the importer's locale (pt-BR/es: '1.234,50'; en: '1,234.50') and converting to the canonical form. The parser has no locale handling. The test is correct.
expectedEvidence: The stack goes from BigDecimal.<init> straight into AmountParser.parse:9.
The comma is the character the message complains about, and the input is a pt-BR formatted amount.
docs/SPEC-i18n.md 'Amount formats': pt-BR and es use dot for thousands and comma for decimals, and the system must accept them.
The plain-decimal test passes, so only the locale format fails.

expectedLimitationsContain: No execution log output was available
retrieval.answerability: Answerable: the cited source, the test and the i18n spec section are all retrieved (the spec through the package prefix of the cited class).

manualChecks: The proposed fix parses according to the importer's locale (for example with NumberFormat/DecimalFormat for the locale), not by stripping every comma and dot blindly.
